name: Koodo Reader
description: Custom Windows updater; 'verification' is just an executable-bit check (fs.accessSync X_OK), no crypto, then spawns the installer.
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: The Windows updater checks only executable permission before spawning the downloaded installer.
limitations: Source-at-commit evidence only; released artifacts and external framework enforcement remain unverified.

original_evidence.text: | Koodo Reader | https://github.com/koodo-reader/koodo-reader.git | 9bb3ec6 / 2026-08-23 | Y (Windows only; macOS/Linux notify-only → opens download webpage externally) | Y (auto version-check on app mount via `checkStableUpdate`/`checkDeveloperUpdate`; the download+install step itself is 1-click, then fully automatic — app quits and silently spawns the installer) | Y (Windows) | https (`dl.koodoreader.com`), TLS enforced (raw Node `https.get`; elsewhere in the same file `rejectUnauthorized: true` is set explicitly for other requests — no disabled-validation code found anywhere) | N (plain JSON version-info response, not a signed manifest) | **None.** `electron-builder`'s config declares a GitHub `publish` provider (which could support `electron-updater`'s signed/checksummed auto-update), but the app never imports `electron-updater`/`autoUpdater` — a fully custom Windows updater downloads `Koodo-Reader-{version}-{arch}.exe` over HTTPS and "verifies" it only by checking the executable-permission bit (`fs.accessSync(path, fs.constants.X_OK)`) — not a cryptographic check of any kind — then spawns it directly and quits | N/A — no cryptographic verification performed (only a POSIX executable-bit check) | `main.js:1351` `ipcMain.handle("update-win-app", …)`; `:1359` hardcoded `https://dl.koodoreader.com/v${version}/...exe`; `:1384-1391` fake "verification" (comment: "验证文件可执行性" / "verify file executability"); `:1397-1403` `spawn(updateExePath, {detached:true, shell:true})` from `app.once("will-quit")`; `src/components/dialogs/updateDialog/component.tsx:36-45` auto-check on mount; `:187` Windows click → `ipcRenderer.invoke("update-win-app", …)`; unused declared provider: `package.json` `build.publish{provider:"github", owner/repo:koodo-reader/koodo-reader}`; TLS not globally disabled: `main.js:1850,1977` `rejectUnauthorized: true` elsewhere |

fields.label: transport
fields.value: https (`dl.koodoreader.com`), TLS enforced (raw Node `https.get`; elsewhere in the same file `rejectUnauthorized: true` is set explicitly for other requests — no disabled-validation code found anywhere)

fields.label: manifest_signed
fields.value: N (plain JSON version-info response, not a signed manifest)

fields.label: payload_verification
fields.value: **None.** `electron-builder`'s config declares a GitHub `publish` provider (which could support `electron-updater`'s signed/checksummed auto-update), but the app never imports `electron-updater`/`autoUpdater` — a fully custom Windows updater downloads `Koodo-Reader-{version}-{arch}.exe` over HTTPS and "verifies" it only by checking the executable-permission bit (`fs.accessSync(path, fs.constants.X_OK)`) — not a cryptographic check of any kind — then spawns it directly and quits

fields.label: verifying_key_source
